correctness.rationale: With t-coordinate beta on N(V), the (v,w) torsion has t-coordinate up to sign beta(v)beta(Tw), so invertibility of T gives beta=0. The (t,t) and (t,v) equations then reduce to ETc=0 and E[T,E]=0, with all other basis pairs automatic. Substituting E=u tensor phi gives phi(Tu)phi=phi(u)(phi composed with T), separating the two stated branches. For each projective functional line a fixed representative gives unique u: in the square-zero branch the two covector constraints allow q^(d-2)-1 nonzero vectors off the eigenlines and q^(d-1)-1 on them, yielding K_T. In the other branch each of H_T/(q-1) lines gives (q-1)q^(d-1) vectors u, and all nonzero E permit q^(d-1) c values. At a=0 count c in ku (q choices in the square-zero branch and one in the eigenline branch) versus off ku to split ranks one and two. At a nonzero, the rank is 1+rank(aI+E); the only singular possibility is the unique a=-phi(u) in the eigenline branch, producing rank d. This yields exactly the displayed polynomial, with coincident degrees combined at d=2, and the corank-one claim is only made for d>=3. The shift M=N-aI has M^2(t)=Ec and M^2(V)=0 in the square-zero branch; index three means phi(c) is nonzero while phi(Tc)=0. This gives q^(d-1)-q^(d-2) c values exactly off the eigenlines, and neither the zero nor eigenline branch contributes. These deductions do not use semisimplicity or a characteristic restriction.
residual_risks: The supplied checker uses selected small cases, not every combination of fields and dimensions mentioned in the verification prose. The conclusions rest on the reviewed algebraic proof, not on extrapolation or formal verification.

value.rationale: The quotient scalar a makes rank(D-aI) an intrinsic stratum of a basic one-generator extension, not an arbitrary subset of matrices. The full rank distribution detects rational eigenlines at corank one for d>=3 and connects them to a different phenomenon, shifted nilpotency of index three, which can occur even when corank one is absent. The formulas hold for nonsemisimple as well as semisimple actions.
residual_risks: There is no classification of higher-rank scalar deviations or conjugacy orbits. The rank-three diagnostic example refers to d=3; the general diagnostic is the rank-d coefficient.
